newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares lower at noon in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares lower at noon in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended slightly lower on Thursday morning in slow trading as foreign investors turned their buying attention to Hong Kong, brokers said.
Surges in recent days in China-related stocks listed in Hong Kong had made that market look more attractive than Shanghai, they said.
The B share index fell 0.413 points or 0.54 percent to 76.553 points on volume of 4.487 million shares worth $1.455 million.
"The B share market is quiet because Hong Kong has surged," said an analyst at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai. "A lot of foreign investors are looking at the H share market."
H shares are shares of Chinese companies listed in the former British colony of Hong Kong, which became a Special Administrative Region of China on July 1.

Sentiment on the B share market was also damaged on Thursday by an editorial in the Financial News, which said China's stock markets had been brought under control by natural market forces, rather than heavy-handed government intervention.
Despite the reassurance from the government about the need to cool the surging stock markets in May, the editorial had spooked some investors, brokers said.
"Companies expected to post good interim results attracted some cautious buying from both overseas investors and domestic players," said a broker at a foreign securities firm.
"But market sentiment is still weak and consolidation will be the main tone in the short term," she said.
Of 45 B shares, 29 traded with 15 down, nine flat and five up.
Plush material maker Shanghai Haixin Co was the biggest B share loser on profit-taking, falling $0.018 or three percent to $0.582.
Shanghai's domestic currency A shares edged up on selective buying, but the mood was cautious due to the Financial News editorial, brokers said.
The A index inched up 5.988 points 0.48 percent to 1,250.899 points on volume of 188.604 million shares worth 2.371 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index rose 38.835 points or 1.01 percent to to 3,883.511 points.
